subject: [PATCH v5 0/7] move stock from mem_cgroup to page_counter

reviews.author: Michal Koutný
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a page_counter is being drained while its stock is still in use, and requested the addition of a check to ensure that the stock is dropped before draining.

Reviewer noted that page_counter_drain_stock_async() may have performance implications and suggested guarding v1 code in drain_all_stock() with !cgroup_on_dfl(memcg->css.cgroup) to mitigate potential issues.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Joshua.

On Mon, Aug 31, 2026 at 09:37:51AM -0700, Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com> wrote:

---

(Just a passerby comment, I have no remarks to the overhaul.)

The change of do_memsw_account() is because of re-attaching the memory
controller between v1 and v2 trees. That's not so common operation (but
not ruled out), pre-condition for that is that there's only a single
online memcg, namely the root memcg. So it needs treatment especially at
memcg offlining (which is what drain_all_stock() (also) does).

I don't know how expensive page_counter_drain_stock_async() is going to
be [1] but the v1 parts here could could be guarded with
!cgroup_on_dfl(memcg->css.cgroup).

Regards,
Michal

[1] Now, I see in 5/7 that there's the counter->stock check which should
    be quick bailout on v2 (maybe quicker than the cgroup_on_dfl()
    Iproposed above).

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged lack of experience with cgroup v1 and recognized the need for guarding, but did not indicate a plan to address this issue in the patch.

Author responded to concerns about performance impact of draining stock, explaining that the function itself is quick and only schedules a job item.

Author responded to reviewer's unclear question about why cgroup_on_dfl() is not present in the code, stating that it should achieve the same goal and was likely omitted for simplicity.
reviews.raw_body:
Wow, that's good to know. To be completely honest I dont have much
experience with cgroup v1. I didn't realize it wasn't a "switch whenever
you want" type of operation. Good to know that there is some more
guarding there.

---

The function itself should be pretty quick. It just frees one CPU's
stock, but the rest is just scheduling a job item.

---

I'm not entirely sure, it's probably similar : -)
I think they should achieve the same goal, and hopefully it wasn't too
difficult to understand why we don't have the cgroup_on_dfl() there.

Hopefully the rest of the code looks good to you too. Thanks again for
taking a look Michal, I hope you have a great day!
Joshua

2026-09-01.patch_summary: This patch series moves the per-cpu 'stock' from mem_cgroup to page_counter, allowing for more efficient and independent stock management. The stock is now a property of each counter rather than the CPU, eliminating the need for cross-memcg interference and random victim eviction. This change also enables transparent charging and refilling of stock through page_counter_try_charge(). As a result, multiple sources of stock management can be added to mem_cgroup without tightly coupling them to struct mem_cgroup.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to a concern about Sashiko's review, stating that they had no concerns with the series and thanking reviewers for their feedback.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Reviewer Shakeel Butt reported a compilation error on GCC 14.2.1 due to missing include directive for the page_counter_stock struct, which is declared as __percpu, requiring an appropriate header to be included.
reviews.raw_body:
On gcc 14.2.1, I get

In file included from mm/page_counter.c:8:
./include/linux/page_counter.h:47:44: error: expected \u2018:\u2019, \u2018,\u2019, \u2018;\u2019, \u2018}\u2019 or \u2018__attribute__\u2019 before \u2018*\u2019 token
   47 |         struct page_counter_stock __percpu *stock;
      |                                            ^

I think you need an appropriate header in this file.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Reviewer Shakeel Butt pointed out that the patch description uses confusing terminology, specifically 'growing the hierarchy size' and 'hierarchy size growth', which should be clarified.
reviews.raw_body:
The terminology of "growing the hierarchy size" and "hierarchy size growth" is
confusing.

The code looks fine.
